liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **So Many Roads** (2 reviews): Reviewer highlights this first-set song as beautiful, noting the madness peaked in the later jam; Jerry reached amazing vocal highs on this track, demonstrating a determined and tight first set performance [12][13]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Described as wild and intense, transitioning sweetly into Uncle John's Band, followed by Vince's finest moment [7]
- **Tomorrow Never Knows** (1 review): Reviewer praises the aggressive dual rhythm transition into Drums, questioning why this arrangement was rare [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **Baba O'Riley**: rare: 12 archived performances [17]
- **Tomorrow Never Knows**: rare: 12 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd94-11-29.schoeps.ladner.10541.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 153 min; rated 2.81/5 by 16 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes the audio as hot, wishing for a better mix to hear Jerry more clearly [6]
- **gd1994-11-29.138022.mgUM70S.graves.flac1648**: source not stated; 18 songs; 152 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1994-11-29.141190.FOB.Schoeps.Clark.Miller.Noel.t-flac1648**: source not stated; 18 songs; 158 min; rated 1/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1994-11-29.154592.AIWA-CM-30A.jwilson.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 152 min [4]

## Around the show

- Jerry left the stage during Easy Answers, while Bobby stepped up with strong jamming performances [6]
- The crowd reacted cheerfully during Baba O'Riley, indicating the band was having fun with the performance [7]
- Reviewer changed into a crazy clown costume in the bathroom before the show, having dropped one item [8]
- Reviewer attended to protect their eight-months-pregnant wife from the crowd, finding the show otherwise weak [9]
- Reviewer was thrown out for sneaking onto the floor, with a Denver cop telling them to go back to Massachusetts [14]
- Reviewer initially walked in the outside corridor but recognized Jerry had life in him during Jack Straw [15]
- Reviewer disagrees with the claim that this was the best show of 1994, citing the 1990 run as excellent [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd94-11-29.schoeps.ladner.10541.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Paul B.; source: Audience: Schoeps MK4's [1]. Also: Audio captured with Schoeps MK4 mics, transferred to DAT then CD, via Paul B, seeded by neolevo [1]
- **gd1994-11-29.138022.mgUM70S.graves.flac1648**: taped by unknown; transferred by Bill Graves; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source: Microtech Gefell UM70S Cards > Teac P-20 > DA-P1; [2]
- **gd1994-11-29.141190.FOB.Schoeps.Clark.Miller.Noel.t-flac1648**: taped by Greg Clark; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: flac16/48kHz ; Master Dat Recording by Greg Clark: (FOB) Schoeps MK41 > Dat (Panasonic SV-255/48k); Transfer info: Dat > Panasonic SV-3700 > Tascam DA-3000 >… [3]
- **gd1994-11-29.154592.AIWA-CM-30A.jwilson.flac16**: taped by Jeff Wilson; transferred by Jeff Wilson; source: AIWA CM-30A mic > Sony WM-D6C [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Michael Mullen Grateful Dead: [1994-11-29 McNichols Sports Arena, Denver, CO, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1994-11-29-mcnichols-sports-arena-denver-co-usa/) [18]
